turns.prompt_text: show me a graph of how wattage affects magnetic force
turns.response_html:
Based on my search, it's not possible to create a single, universally applicable graph of how wattage affects magnetic force because the relationship is not simple and depends on the specific characteristics of the electromagnet, such as its resistance and design.

However, I can explain the general relationship based on the physics:

  • The magnetic field strength ($B$) is directly proportional to the current ($I$) flowing through the electromagnet's coil.
  • The magnetic force ($F$) is proportional to the square of the magnetic field strength, so $F \propto B^2$. This means that the force is also proportional to the square of the current ($F \propto I^2$).
  • Electrical power (wattage), is given by the formula $P = I^2 \times R$, where $R$ is the resistance of the coil.

From these relationships, we can see that both the magnetic force and the power are proportional to the square of the current ($F \propto I^2$ and $P \propto I^2$). This implies that for a given electromagnet, the magnetic force is directly proportional to the power. So, if you were to double the wattage, the magnetic force would also double (assuming the resistance and other factors remain constant).
